paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 31:14-16: “This condition is the condition of the Exodus from Egypt, of which it is said, ‘For the people fled.’ At first sight this is puzzling: why was it so? Had they told Pharaoh to release them forever, would he not have been compelled to release them? Rather, the evil in the souls of Israel was still at full strength in the left chamber, for their impurity did not cease until the giving of the Torah. Their aim and desire were only that their divine soul should leave the exile of the other side, which is the impurity of Egypt, and cleave to Him, blessed be He. As it is written, ‘Hashem, my strength, my stronghold, and my refuge in a day of distress,’ and so forth; ‘my stronghold and my refuge,’ and so forth; ‘He is a refuge for me,’ and so forth. Therefore, in the future, when Hashem removes the spirit of impurity from the earth, it is written, ‘You shall not go in flight, for Hashem goes before you,’ and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Human Dispositions 3:3: “Someone who conducts himself according to medicine, but intends only that his body and limbs should be sound and that he should have children to perform his work and labor for his needs, is not following a good path. Rather, he should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul may be upright in knowing Hashem, for one cannot understand and contemplate wisdom while hungry or ill, or while one of his limbs is in pain. He should intend to have a son who may become wise and great in Israel. Thus, one who follows this path throughout his life serves Hashem continually, even while doing business and even during marital relations, because his intention in everything is to obtain what he needs so that his body will be sound for serving Hashem. Even while sleeping, if he sleeps deliberately so that his mind and body may rest, lest he become ill and be unable to serve Hashem because of his illness, his sleep is service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this, the Sages commanded, ‘Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.’ This is what Solomon said in his wisdom: ‘Know Him in all your ways, and He will make your paths straight.’”

paragraphs.text: Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Vayikra 16: “I heard from my master, my grandfather, of blessed memory, concerning the verse ‘Fortunate is the person to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity’: his thought is continually attached to the blessed Hashem. Therefore, when he falls away from that thought for a single moment and does not think of Hashem, he regards it as iniquity and sin. This is ‘Fortunate is the person who does not think of Hashem’: when he does not think of Hashem, ‘it is iniquity for him’—it is an iniquity in his eyes. This is a sign that his thought is continually attached to the blessed Hashem, and therefore fortunate is he.”

This is ‘Fortunate is the person who does not think of Hashem’: when he does not think of Hashem, ‘it is iniquity for him’—it is an iniquity in his eyes. This is a sign that his thought is continually attached to the blessed Hashem, and therefore fortunate is he.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 1: “‘They shall wash their hands and feet.’ The priests’ washing from the laver signifies the removal and elimination of personal bias. Washing indicates this, as it is written concerning the heifer whose neck is broken: ‘The elders shall wash,’ and so forth, ‘and say: Our hands did not shed,’ and so forth. They declare that they have no personal involvement or share in this deed. The priest who serves also needs washing: he must remove his personal bias and nullify his judgment and will before the will of the blessed Hashem, serving only in the way that Hashem desires. So too, our command to wash our hands in the morning and before a meal means that before beginning to attend to bodily needs, a person needs to pray to Hashem. If something of this world comes to him that is, Heaven forbid, contrary to Hashem’s will, he asks Hashem to take away and remove his desire for it. Even a permitted thing contains good and its opposite. If a person eats something permitted and afterward uses that strength to commit a transgression, it becomes apparent that he did not receive the good power contained in that thing. This is the purpose of washing: a prayer to Hashem that, in everything, he receive only the good power it contains. For a person may stipulate concerning an inheritance coming to him from elsewhere that he will not inherit it. For this reason, they established the recitation of the passage of the laver before prayer and before the passages of the offerings: that we should pray only for what Hashem desires.”

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Immersion Pools 11:12: “It is clear and evident that the laws of impurity and purity are decrees of Scripture. They are not matters decided by human reason; they belong among the statutes. Immersion from impurity likewise belongs among the statutes, for impurity is not mud or filth that water can remove. It is a decree of Scripture, and the matter depends on the heart’s intention. Therefore the Sages said: if one immersed without establishing the intended degree of purification, it is as though he had not immersed. Nevertheless, there is an allusion in this matter. Just as one who intends in his heart to purify himself becomes pure upon immersion, although nothing has changed in his body, so one who intends to purify his soul from the impurities of the soul—wicked thoughts and evil opinions—becomes pure once he resolves in his heart to separate from those counsels and brings his soul into the waters of knowledge. Scripture says: ‘I shall sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall become pure; from all your impurities and all your idols I shall purify you.’ May Hashem, in His abundant mercy, purify us from every sin, iniquity, and guilt. Amen.”

paragraphs.text: Ya'arot Devash, Part II, Sermon 2: “The Gemara in Gittin says: ‘One who sells his slave to a gentile, when he has made his nimos for him,’ and so forth. It asks: What is nimos? A nashka. Rashi explains: a seal that a master fastens upon his slave as a sign that he belongs to him. So it is with us: we are Hashem’s servants, and the seal that the Master of all the earth has fastened upon us, as a sign that we are His servants, is tefillin and tzitzit. They are the seal of our Master in heaven, our nimos that we have from the Holy One, blessed be He. It is unfitting to walk without this seal, for these are the sign that we are servants of the Holy One, blessed be He.”

paragraphs.text:
Mesillat Yesharim 17:6-8: “Among the practices that guide a person toward attaining this trait is preparation for divine service and the commandments. That is, one should not begin performing a commandment suddenly, before the mind is settled and able to reflect on what one is doing. Rather, one should prepare for it and ready the heart calmly until one enters into reflection.

Then one should consider what one is about to do and before Whom one is about to do it. For once one enters into this reflection, it is easy to cast off ulterior motives and establish in the heart the true and desired intention.

You see that the early pious ones would wait an hour before their prayer and then pray, so that they might direct their hearts toward the Omnipresent. Certainly they did not spend an hour idly. Rather, they directed and prepared their hearts for the prayer they were to offer, casting away foreign thoughts and filling themselves with the requisite awe and love. Scripture says: ‘If you prepare your heart and spread your hands toward Him’ (Job 11:13).”

וּמִן הַמַּעֲשִׂים הַמַּדְרִיכִים אֶת הָאָדָם לָבוֹא לִידֵי מִדָּה זוֹ, הוּא הַהַזְמָנָה לְדִבְרֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה וְהַמִּצְוֹת, וְהַיְנוּ, שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס בְּקִיּוּם הַמִּצְוָה בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאוֹם שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ עֲדַיִן מְיֻשֶּׁבֶת עָלָיו וִיכוֹלָה לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּמָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה, אֶלָּא יַזְמִין עַצְמוֹ לַדָּבָר וְיָכִין לִבּוֹ בְּמִתּוּן עַד שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס בְּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת.

וְאָז יִתְבּוֹנֵן מָה הוּא הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת וְלִפְנֵי מִי הוּא הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת, שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּהִכָּנְסוֹ בָּעִיּוּן הַזֶּה, קַל הוּא שֶׁיַּשְׁלִיךְ מֵעָלָיו הַפְּנִיּוֹת הַחִיצוֹנִיּוֹת וְיִקְבַּע בְּלִבּוֹ הַכַּוָּנָה הָאֲמִתִּית הָרְצוּיָה.

וְתִרְאֶה שֶׁהַחֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִים שָׁעָה אַחַת קֹדֶם תְּפִלָּתָם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְפַּלְּלִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּנוּ לִבָּם לַמָּקוֹם. וּבְוַדַּאי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ פּוֹנִים שָׁעָה אַחַת לְבַטָּלָה, אֶלָּא מִתְכַּוְּנִים וּמְכִינִים לִבָּם לַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל, וְדוֹחִים מֵעֲלֵיהֶם הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת הַזָּרוֹת וּמִתְמַלְּאִים הַיִּרְאָה וְהָאַהֲבָה הַצְּרִיכָה, וְאוֹמֵר (איוב יא): אִם אַתָּה הֲכִינוֹתָ לִבֶּךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ אֵלָיו כַּפֶּיךָ.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berakhot 2a:3: “In the Gemara: ‘What is the tanna referring to when he teaches “From when”?’ It answers: ‘The tanna refers to Scripture.’ Rabbi’s compilation of the Mishnah was not separated from the Written Torah by any division or distance. Just as the tannaim and amoraim of the Gemara studied the Mishnah, sought to understand its meaning, and explained it, so the compilation of the Mishnah was based on the Written Torah. When he studied the verse ‘when you lie down and when you rise,’ he immediately explained the time for reciting the Shema. In this way he arranged the entire Mishnah.”

quotation.he: בגמרא תנא היכא קאי דקתני מאימתי ומשני תנא אקרא קאי. היינו שלא נפרד חיבר משניות של רבי בשום פרוד והפרש מתורה שבכתב, רק כמו שהגמרא למדו התנאים והאמוראים את המשניות ורצו לעמד על דעת המשניות ופרשו אותם, כן חיבר המשנה היה על תורה שבכתב, בעת שלמד הפסוק "בשכבך ובקומך" אז פירש תיכף זמן קריאת שמע, וכן סידר כל המשניות.
quotation.en: In the Gemara: ‘What is the tanna referring to when he teaches “From when”?’ It answers: ‘The tanna refers to Scripture.’ Rabbi’s compilation of the Mishnah was not separated from the Written Torah by any division or distance. Just as the tannaim and amoraim of the Gemara studied the Mishnah, sought to understand its meaning, and explained it, so the compilation of the Mishnah was based on the Written Torah. When he studied the verse ‘when you lie down and when you rise,’ he immediately explained the time for reciting the Shema. In this way he arranged the entire Mishnah.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part III; Iggeret HaTeshuvah 2:1-3: “All this concerns atonement and forgiveness of the sin: when a person repents completely, his past violation of the King’s command is wholly forgiven. Not a thing or half a thing is mentioned against him on the day of judgment to punish him for it, Heaven forbid, in the World to Come, and he is entirely released from judgment in the World to Come. However, to be acceptable before Hashem, pleasing and beloved before Him as before the sin, so that his service brings satisfaction to his Maker, he needed to bring a burnt offering even for a minor positive commandment involving neither excision nor execution by the court. So our Sages expounded in the Sifra on the verse ‘It shall be accepted for him’; and so it is stated in the first chapter of Zevachim: a burnt offering atones for a positive commandment and is a gift after a person has repented and his punishment has been forgiven. It is like someone who offended a king, appeased him through advocates, and was pardoned: nevertheless, he sends a gift and tribute so that the king will consent to receive him. The expression ‘atones,’ and Scripture’s words ‘It shall be accepted for him, to atone for him,’ do not mean atonement for his soul, but atonement before Hashem, bringing satisfaction to his Maker, as stated there in the Gemara and as it is written, ‘It shall be unblemished to be accepted.’”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: אך כל זה לענין כפרה ומחילת העון, שנמחל לו לגמרי מה שעבר על מצות המלך כשעשה תשובה שלימה, ואין מזכירין לו דבר וחצי דבר ביום הדין לענשו על זה חס ושלום בעולם־הבא, ונפטר לגמרי מן הדין בעולם־הבא. אמנם, שיהיה לרצון לפני ה׳ ומרוצה וחביב לפניו יתברך כקודם החטא, להיות נחת רוח לקונו מעבודתו – היה צריך להביא קרבן עולה אפילו על מצות עשה קלה שאין בה כרת ומיתת בית־דין, כמו שדרשו רבותינו־זכרונם־לברכה בתורת כהנים על פסוק ״ונרצה לו״; וכדאיתא בגמרא פרק קמא דזבחים, דעולה מכפרת על מצות עשה, והיא דורון לאחר שעשה תשובה ונמחל לו העונש. וכאדם שסרח במלך ופייסו על־ידי פרקליטין ומחל לו, אף־על־פי־כן, שולח דורון ומנחה לפניו שיתרצה לו לראות פני המלך (ולשון ״מכפרת״, וכן מה שכתוב בתורה ״ונרצה לו לכפר עליו״ – אין זו כפרת נפשו, אלא לכפר לפני ה׳ להיות נחת רוח לקונו, כדאיתא שם בגמרא, וכמו שכתוב: ״תמים יהיה לרצון״).

paragraphs.text: Tosefta Peah 3:13: “There was an incident involving a pious man who forgot a sheaf in his field. He said to his son, ‘Go and offer a bull as a burnt offering and a bull as a peace offering on my behalf.’ His son said to him, ‘Father, what led you to rejoice over this commandment more than over all the other commandments in the Torah?’ He replied, ‘The Omnipresent gave us all the commandments in the Torah to fulfill knowingly, but this one unknowingly. Had we done it intentionally before the Omnipresent, this commandment would not have come into our hands. Rather, Scripture says, “When you reap,” and so forth: Scripture assigns him a blessing. The argument follows all the more strongly: if one who did not intend to acquire merit nevertheless acquired it and is credited as meritorious, how much more so one who intended to acquire merit and acquired it! Similarly, “If a person sins and does,” and so forth, “he shall bring an unblemished ram,” and so forth. The argument follows all the more strongly: if one who did not intend to sin nevertheless sinned and is regarded as having sinned, how much more so one who intended to sin and sinned!’”

paragraphs.text: Rosh on Berakhot 1:2:1: “Gemara: ‘Until the end of the first watch’—these are Rabbi Eliezer’s words. We conclude that he holds that the night has three watches. He does not say ‘a third of the night’ because he teaches another matter along the way: there are watches in heaven just as there are watches on earth. For it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says that the night has three watches, and at each watch the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and roars like a lion, as it is said, ‘Hashem will roar from on high, and from His holy dwelling,’ and so forth, ‘He will roar mightily over His abode.’ It was also stated: Rav Shmuel bar Marta said in Rav’s name that the night has three watches, and at each watch the Holy One, blessed be He, says, ‘Woe to My children, for because of their sins I destroyed My house, burned My sanctuary, and exiled them among the nations of the world.’ Every person who fears Heaven should therefore grieve and be concerned at that hour and pour out supplications over the destruction of the Temple, as it is said, ‘Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches.’”

after.enAnchorPrefix: and so too the obscurity of light, and so too the prolonged era of exile, is subdivided into these three developmental phases, as I explained elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: Netzach Yisrael 18:14-15: “The night is divided into three watches, as stated in the first chapter of Berakhot: it was taught that Rabbi Eliezer says the night has three watches, and at every watch the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and roars like a lion, as it is said, ‘Hashem will roar from on high; He will roar mightily over His abode.’ The signs are: in the first watch a donkey brays; in the second, dogs cry; in the third, an infant nurses from its mother and a wife speaks with her husband. One must ask why at every watch the Holy One, blessed be He, cries, ‘Woe to Me, for I have destroyed My house,’ and so forth. Know that night is darkness and resembles exile, in which Israel sits in darkness without light. Thus, when Israel was redeemed, it is written, ‘The Jews had light.’ Night is therefore a sign of exile. Just as night divides into three watches, exile divides into three parts, corresponding exactly to the watches of the night, which signify the three parts of exile. Therefore the blessed Hashem sits and cries at every watch, ‘Woe to Me, for I have destroyed My house,’ and so forth. At the beginning of exile, they placed a yoke upon Israel and made the exile exceedingly burdensome. Israel constantly bore a great yoke and burden, like a donkey bearing a heavy load. This was how they acted at the beginning of exile, under the Babylonian kingdom; such was its first part. The second part of exile was a generation of persecution, when decrees of death and apostasy were imposed upon them. This corresponds to the second watch, when dogs cry. Dogs crying is a sign of death, as the Sages said: when dogs cry, the angel of death has come to the city. So in the second part of exile they killed and put Jews to death. Therefore it says, ‘In the second watch, dogs cry,’ a sign of lamentation and death; over this too the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and roars like a lion. In the third part of exile there is no such persecution—may Hashem protect His people Israel from it—and the nations treat Israel as a husband treats a wife. For the nations are considered Israel’s husbands in exile, as it is said, ‘Lords other than You have ruled over us.’ When a wife finds no favor in her husband’s eyes, he divorces her. So the nations expel Israel when Israel finds no favor in their eyes. This is the principal feature of exile’s third part. Concerning it he said, ‘In the third watch, a wife speaks with her husband.’ He also said that in the third watch an infant nurses from its mother. Correspondingly, at the end of exile Israel, considered infants in Torah, nurse from their mother’s breasts—from the earlier sages, who are called their mother. This is because they were given no rest to settle in one place, but wandered from place to place, until, because of our many sins, Torah was entirely forgotten from Israel through the exile.”

paragraphs.text:
Maggid Devarav leYaakov 13:5: “When a person needs to ask the Creator, blessed be He, for something, he should think that his soul is, as it were, a limb of the Shekhinah, like a drop from the sea. He should pray on behalf of the Shekhinah, for that thing is lacking in the Shekhinah, and he should have faith that he is certainly bringing about an effect above for the Shekhinah. Only if he is properly attached to the Shekhinah will the abundance also be drawn upon him.

This is like a person who experiences joy and claps his hands even without intending to, because the joy spreads into the limb. So it is here: since he is, as it were, a limb of the Shekhinah, the abundance will also be drawn upon him. He should think that he is only a vessel, and that his thought and speech are worlds that extend forth. The world of speech, which is the Shekhinah, petitions the world of thought concerning these words. When he draws the light of the Creator, blessed be He, into his thought and speech, his request should be that abundance spread from the world of thought to the world of speech. It will also come into the matter he is speaking about, which he needs, and his request will be granted. This is the meaning of ‘Be found by us in our beseeching’: that He, blessed be He, should be found within those requests.”

quotation.he: כשצריך לבקש איזה דבר מהבורא ית' יחשוב שנשמתו הוא אבר מהשכינה כביכול כטפה מן הים ויבקש על השכינה שאותו דבר הוא חסר להשכינה ויהי' לו האמנה שבוודאי הוא פועל מלמעלה להשכינה. רק אם יהיה דבוק כראוי אל השכינה יתמשך גם כן השפע עליו. כמשל אדם שיש לו שמחה מטפח ביד אפילו כשאינו מתכוין לכך מחמת שהשמחה מתפשטת באבר כן הוא בענין זה שהוא אבר מהשכינה כביכול יתמשך גם כן השפע עליו ויחשוב שהוא אינו רק כלי ומחשבתו ודיבורו הם עולמות שמתפשטים עולם הדיבור שהוא השכינה מבקשת מעולם המחשבה על דבורים האלו וכשימשיך אור הבורא ית' במחשבתו ודיבורו יהיה בקשתו שיתפשט השפע מעולם המחשבה אל עולם הדיבור ויבא ג"כ באותו ענין שהוא מדבר שצריך לו ויעשה לו בקשתו. וזהו המצא לנו בבקשתינו שיהיה הוא ית' נמצא באותן הבקשות.
quotation.en:
When a person needs to ask the Creator, blessed be He, for something, he should think that his soul is, as it were, a limb of the Shekhinah, like a drop from the sea. He should pray on behalf of the Shekhinah, for that thing is lacking in the Shekhinah, and he should have faith that he is certainly bringing about an effect above for the Shekhinah. Only if he is properly attached to the Shekhinah will the abundance also be drawn upon him.

This is like a person who experiences joy and claps his hands even without intending to, because the joy spreads into the limb. So it is here: since he is, as it were, a limb of the Shekhinah, the abundance will also be drawn upon him. He should think that he is only a vessel, and that his thought and speech are worlds that extend forth. The world of speech, which is the Shekhinah, petitions the world of thought concerning these words. When he draws the light of the Creator, blessed be He, into his thought and speech, his request should be that abundance spread from the world of thought to the world of speech. It will also come into the matter he is speaking about, which he needs, and his request will be granted. This is the meaning of ‘Be found by us in our beseeching’: that He, blessed be He, should be found within those requests.

paragraphs.text: Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Matot 4: “‘Arm men from among you for the army, that they may go against Midian,’ and so forth, ‘to execute Hashem’s vengeance upon Midian.’ One may explain this by allusion, following what I heard from my relative by marriage, the venerable, departed Rabbi Nachman of Horodenka, of blessed memory, concerning the verse ‘No man shall ascend with you on that entire mountain.’ When a person wishes to serve Hashem truly and wholeheartedly, he must think and imagine himself as though he alone exists in the world, without any ulterior consideration arising from another person. On this basis I explained, ‘No person shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he enters to atone in the holy place’; understand this. This is also the meaning of ‘Where there are no people, strive to be a man’: strive always to be as though in a place without people. This may also be hinted at here: ‘Arm yourselves’ can mean ‘remove’—remove people from yourselves, as in ‘No man shall ascend with you.’ Fight only Hashem’s battle against Midian, for no human purpose, Heaven forbid, but solely to execute Hashem’s vengeance upon Midian. Understand this.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: And as written in Sefer Toledot Yaakov Yosef on the verse "The pious man has ceased, for the faithful fail" (Psalms 12:2) in the name of Rabbi Leib Pistiner, that this verse may be expounded from its beginning to its end, and from its end to its beginning.

paragraphs.text: Toldot Yaakov Yosef, Shemot 2-3: “It appears to me in accordance with what I explained about the passage in Arakhin: ‘I wonder whether there is anyone in this generation who knows how to rebuke’; see there. I heard from the departed Rabbi Yehudah Leib of Pistina an explanation of the verse ‘Save, Hashem, for the pious person has ceased, for the faithful have vanished from among mankind.’ The pious person has ceased because the faithful have vanished from mankind: one draws the other along, because of their unity. He was told in a dream that perhaps the meaning is the reverse: because the pious person has ceased, the faithful have vanished from mankind. His words are words from the mouth of a wise person, gracious words. Accordingly I explained the verse ‘Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins.’ Tell ‘My people,’ the Torah scholars, that their transgression caused the faithful to vanish from mankind. Tell ‘the house of Jacob,’ the ordinary people, that their sins caused the pious person to cease. Thus each should attribute the sin and deficiency to himself rather than to his fellow.”

paragraphs.text: Yosher Divrei Emet, Second Kuntres 34:2: “I heard a fine parable concerning this from the departed righteous Rabbi Yissachar Ber of our community, who related it in the name of his teacher, Rabbi Mendel. Suppose a company of many people are traveling on foot to a certain place, and one of them, Heaven forbid, falls ill. They must continue their journey. Surely they will not leave him there to perish; if he cannot walk, they will take him by the arms and lead him. But if, Heaven forbid, one of them dies, what use have they for a dead person? They will bury him there. The application is this: when speech is united with thought, even without fear and love, it is like a sick person who has a little life, and the righteous will assist it, as explained above. But without any thought at all, it is considered dead, Heaven forbid, and is thrown onto the refuse heap. He added: even if, Heaven forbid, this is its condition, such prayers still fulfill the King’s will when nothing else is possible, for the King also needs dogs and their sustenance is His responsibility. These are the wholly unfit prayers. Yet this is no reason for us to choose to provide the dogs’ portion; it is better for us to give nourishment to the King Himself, or at least to His close servants, the holy worlds.”

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Repentance 5:5: “You may ask: Does the Holy One, blessed be He, not know all that will happen? Before it happens, does He know that this person will be righteous or wicked, or does He not know? If He knows that the person will be righteous, it is impossible for him not to be righteous; and if you say that He knows he will be righteous but he may be wicked, then He does not know the matter clearly. Know that the answer to this question is longer than the earth and broader than the sea; many great principles and lofty mountains depend upon it. But you must know and understand what I say here. We have already explained in the second chapter of the Laws of the Foundations of the Torah that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not know through a knowledge external to Himself, as human beings and their knowledge are two things. Rather, He, exalted be His name, and His knowledge are one, and human understanding cannot grasp this matter fully. Just as a person cannot grasp and discover the truth of the Creator, as it is said, ‘A person cannot see Me and live,’ so a person cannot grasp and discover the Creator’s knowledge. This is what the prophet said: ‘My thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not My ways.’ Since this is so, we lack the power to know how the Holy One, blessed be He, knows all creatures and deeds. Nevertheless, we know without doubt that a person’s action lies in his own hands, and the Holy One, blessed be He, neither draws him nor decrees that he act in a particular way. We know this not only from received religion but also through clear rational proofs. Therefore prophecy says that a person is judged for his actions according to what he has done, whether good or evil. This is the principle upon which all the words of prophecy depend.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: שמא תאמר והלא הקדוש ברוך הוא יודע כל מה שיהיה וקדם שיהיה ידע שזה יהיה צדיק או רשע או לא ידע. אם ידע שהוא יהיה צדיק אי אפשר שלא יהיה צדיק ואם תאמר שידע שיהיה צדיק ואפשר שיהיה רשע הרי לא ידע הדבר על בריו. דע שתשובת שאלה זו ארכה מארץ מדה ורחבה מני ים וכמה עקרים גדולים והררים רמים תלויים בה אבל צריך אתה לידע ולהבין בדבר זה שאני אומר. כבר בארנו בפרק שני מהלכות יסודי התורה שהקדוש ברוך הוא אינו יודע מדעה שהיא חוץ ממנו כבני אדם שהם ודעתם שנים. אלא הוא יתעלה שמו ודעתו אחד ואין דעתו של אדם יכולה להשיג דבר זה על בריו. וכשם שאין כח באדם להשיג ולמצא אמתת הבורא שנאמר (שמות לג כ) "כי לא יראני האדם וחי" כך אין כח באדם להשיג ולמצא דעתו של הבורא. הוא שהנביא אמר (ישעיה נה ח) "כי לא מחשבותי מחשבותיכם ולא דרכיכם דרכי". וכיון שכן הוא אין בנו כח לידע היאך ידע הקדוש ברוך הוא כל הברואים והמעשים אבל נדע בלא ספק שמעשה האדם ביד האדם ואין הקדוש ברוך הוא מושכו ולא גוזר עליו לעשות כך. ולא מפני קבלת הדת בלבד נודע דבר זה אלא בראיות ברורות מדברי החכמה. ומפני זה נאמר בנבואה שדנין את האדם על מעשיו כפי מעשיו אם טוב ואם רע וזה הוא העקר שכל דברי הנבואה תלויין בו:

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Leviticus 16:8: “The intention concerning the scapegoat is not, Heaven forbid, that it should be an offering from us to him. Rather, our intention is to fulfill the will of our Creator, who commanded us to do so. The analogy is someone who prepares a feast for a master, and the master tells the person preparing it, ‘Give one portion to such-and-such servant of mine.’ The person preparing the feast gives nothing of his own to that servant and does not act in his honor. Everything was given to the master; the master gives a portion to his servant, while this person keeps his command and does all that he commanded in the master’s honor. The master, in compassion for the host, wished all his servants to enjoy the feast, so that they would speak his praise and not his disparagement. This is the reason for the lots. Had the priest verbally consecrated the goats to Hashem and to Azazel, he would have been like someone worshipping him and making a vow in his name. Instead, he placed them before Hashem at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, for both are a gift to Hashem. He gives His servant the portion that comes to him from Hashem: He cast their lot and His hand apportioned it to them, as it is said, ‘The lot is cast into the lap, but all its judgment is from Hashem.’ Even after the lot, he would place the goat before Hashem, to declare that it belongs to Him and that in sending it we intend only to fulfill Hashem’s will, as it says, ‘It shall stand alive before Hashem, to atone over it and send it,’ and so forth. For this reason, we do not slaughter it at all.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: ואין הכונה בשעיר המשתלח שיהיה קרבן מאתנו אליו חלילה, אבל שתהיה כונתנו לעשות רצון בוראנו שצונו כך. והמשל בזה כמי שעשה סעודה לאדון וצוה האדון את האיש העושה הסעודה תן מנה אחת לעבדי פלוני, שאין העושה הסעודה נותן כלום לעבד ההוא ולא לכבודו יעשה עמו, רק הכל נתן לאדון והאדון נותן פרס לעבדו, ושמר זה מצותו ועשה לכבוד האדון כל אשר צוהו. ואמנם האדון לחמלתו על בעל הסעודה רצה שיהיו כל עבדיו נהנין ממנה, שיספר בשבחו ולא בגנותו. וזה טעם הגורלות, כי אלו היה הכהן מקדיש אותם בפה לה' ולעזאזל היה כעובד אליו ונודר לשמו, אבל היה מעמיד אתם לפני ה' פתח אהל מועד (ויקרא ט"ז:ז'), כי שניהם מתנה לה', והוא נתן מהם לעבדו החלק אשר יבא לו מאת השם, הוא הפיל להם גורל וידו חלק להם, כענין שנאמר (משלי טז לג) "בחיק יוטל את הגורל ומה' כל משפטו", וגם אחרי הגורל היה מעמידו לפני ה', לומר שהוא שלו ואין אנחנו מכונים בשלוחו אלא לרצון לשם, כמו שאמר (ויקרא ט"ז:י') "יעמד חי לפני ה' לכפר עליו לשלח אתו" וגו', ולכך לא נשחוט אותו אנחנו כלל.

Rather, our intention is to fulfill the will of our Creator, who commanded us to do so. The analogy is someone who prepares a feast for a master, and the master tells the person preparing it, ‘Give one portion to such-and-such servant of mine.’ The person preparing the feast gives nothing of his own to that servant and does not act in his honor. Everything was given to the master; the master gives a portion to his servant, while this person keeps his command and does all that he commanded in the master’s honor. The master, in compassion for the host, wished all his servants to enjoy the feast, so that they would speak his praise and not his disparagement. This is the reason for the lots. Had the priest verbally consecrated the goats to Hashem and to Azazel, he would have been like someone worshipping him and making a vow in his name. Instead, he placed them before Hashem at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, for both are a gift to Hashem. He gives His servant the portion that comes to him from Hashem: He cast their lot and His hand apportioned it to them, as it is said, ‘The lot is cast into the lap, but all its judgment is from Hashem.’ Even after the lot, he would place the goat before Hashem, to declare that it belongs to Him and that in sending it we intend only to fulfill Hashem’s will, as it says, ‘It shall stand alive before Hashem, to atone over it and send it,’ and so forth. For this reason, we do not slaughter it at all.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Miketz 2:1: “As we heard from our holy master, of blessed memory, on the verse, “The Rock of Israel spoke to me: a righteous one rules over man, ruling through the fear of God”: “Rock” denotes firmness. Hashem gives firmness to the penitent’s heart, as though He had spoken to him personally, enabling him to rule over a righteous man. This means that even concerning matters of which Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said in the holy Zohar that repentance is ineffective, Heaven forbid, the penitent has the power to annul that judgment and repair them. “Ruling through the fear of God” also includes what was spoken by the Holy One, blessed be He, as when a heavenly voice declared, “Return, wayward children, except Acher.” Nevertheless, he could have repaired himself through repentance, because this is Hashem’s will. As the Shelah and Reishit Chokhmah wrote, this is what the Sages hinted at: “Do everything the master of the house tells you, except ‘Leave.’””

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 16:5: “The moment of the inclination’s enticement between one spiritual level and another is the descent that the righteous undergo for the sake of ascent, as is known concerning “A righteous person falls seven times and rises.” This was the meaning of Rephidim after the splitting of the sea, when they were proceeding to the giving of the Torah, a higher level. When a person succeeds in overcoming it immediately, the descent is scarcely felt at all: he falls for only a moment and rises at once. There is only a momentary slackening; he immediately remembers, takes it to heart, and strengthens himself like a lion for Hashem’s service. The greater the subsequent ascent, however, the greater the preceding descent. For a great ascent the inclination grows stronger, one corresponding to the other, and the power that overcomes it is correspondingly greater.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 28:1: “For in the end Israel is redeemed only through repentance, and they will prevail in their plea, “Return us to You,” so that even the awakening to repentance comes from Hashem. paragraphs.text: Niddah 14a: ‘The baraita continues: As for donkey drivers, some of them are wicked while some of them are righteous. With regard to the difference between wicked and righteous donkey drivers, there are those who say that this donkey driver is righteous, as his donkey is saddled, and therefore his penis does not rub against it, whereas that donkey driver is wicked, as his donkey is not saddled, which can cause a seminal emission. And there are those who say: This donkey driver is wicked, as he spreads [demittartein] his thighs on either side of the donkey, whereas that donkey driver is righteous as he does not spread his thighs in this manner, but rides with both legs on one side of the donkey, so that his penis does not rub against the donkey.’

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 3:2: “Nevertheless, the counsel is, “Feed him,” for “you are heaping coals upon his head”: ultimately the words of Torah will benefit the person. Although the evil inclination supposes that it will draw nourishment from Torah studied for ulterior motives, a person should still always engage in it, for from study for ulterior motives one comes to study for its own sake. The Midrash says, “If only they had abandoned Me but kept My Torah, for through occupying themselves with it, the light within it would have brought them back to the good”—that is, they would come to study for its own sake, as explained concerning Rosh Chodesh Kislev. This is as we explained concerning the statements, “Bring water to meet the thirsty” and “Let everyone who is thirsty go to the water”: when the student is worthy, the teacher should go to him; otherwise, “Let everyone who is thirsty go to the water.” Although a teacher is not obliged to teach an unworthy student, Scripture counsels the student himself to go to the water, for from study for ulterior motives he will come to study for its own sake, and the light within it brings him back to the good.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 59b: ‘The Gemara further relates: Imma Shalom, the wife of Rabbi Eliezer, was the sister of Rabban Gamliel. From that incident forward, she would not allow Rabbi Eliezer to lower his head and recite the taḥanun prayer, which includes supplication and entreaties. She feared that were her husband to bemoan his fate and pray at that moment, her brother would be punished. A certain day was around the day of the New Moon, and she inadvertently substituted a full thirty-day month for a deficient twenty-nine-day month, i.e., she thought that it was the New Moon, when one does not lower his head in supplication, but it was not. Some say that a pauper came and stood at the door, and she took bread out to him. The result was that she left her husband momentarily unsupervised.’

quotation.he: ואף שכבר עשה תשובה נכונה, הרי עיקר התשובה – בלב, והלב, יש בו בחינות ומדרגות רבות, והכל לפי מה שהוא אדם, ולפי הזמן והמקום, כידוע ליודעים. ולכן, עכשיו בשעה זו, שרואה בעצמו דלא סליק ביה נהורא דנשמתא, מכלל, שהיום לא נתקבלה תשובתו, ועונותיו מבדילים, או, שרוצים להעלותו לתשובה עילאה יותר, מעומקא דלבא יותר. ולכן אמר דוד: ״וחטאתי נגדי תמיד״.
quotation.en: Even though he has already repented properly, the essence of repentance is in the heart, and the heart has many levels and degrees. Everything depends on the person as he is, and on the time and place, as those who understand know. Therefore, now, at this moment, when he sees that the light of his soul does not rise within him, this indicates that today his repentance has not been accepted and his sins separate him, or that they wish to raise him to a higher repentance, from a still deeper place in his heart. Therefore David said, “My sin is before me always.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Teshuvah 1:49: “The nineteenth principle is abandoning his sin when it presents itself to him and his desire is at its strongest. Our Sages of blessed memory said: Who is a penitent whose repentance reaches the Throne of Glory? One who is tested and emerges innocent at the same stage, in the same place, and with the same woman. This means that the sin presented itself to him while his inclination and physical vigor were as strong as at the first time when he sinned, yet he subdued his inclination and escaped the transgression out of fear of the Lord and dread of His majesty. If such an occasion has not presented itself to him, he should increase the fear of the Lord within himself day by day, throughout his life. When he renews the strength of that fear sufficiently to subdue his inclination and the force of its rule at the height of desire, surely He who searches hearts understands, and He who guards his soul knows, that if he were to face a test and encounter the same situation as before, he would save himself from his inclination. He thus stands before the Lord on the highest level of repentance.”

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 19:13: “That is why he was descended from converts: openly manifest love of Torah is found especially among converts. For the Holy One, blessed be He, brought the children of Israel out of slavery to freedom and made them a kingdom of priests. After all this He brought them before Mount Sinai—He drew them close and suspended the mountain over them like a barrel (Shabbat 88a). Even when they accepted it again out of love in the days of Ahasuerus, this arose from love for the miracle and deliverance. But a convert has left behind the ease of this world and the unrestricted pursuit of desires that he had among the nations. Of his own will he comes to restrain himself and to join Israel, who are afflicted, lowly, and hard pressed in this world. For “in your poverty he will fall to you,” and converts were not accepted in the days of David and Solomon, nor someone who converts out of love for some other thing (Yevamot 24b). Solely out of love for Torah he draws himself near and places himself under the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: And a found treasure, our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 97a), comes only through distraction of the mind;

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 10:3: “Thus it is taught in Megillah 6b: “If one says, ‘I did not labor and I found,’ do not believe him.” Labor must come first, yet afterward it is still called “I found,” and a found object comes when one’s attention is diverted (Sanhedrin 97a). For Torah truly lies beyond human comprehension, and all a person’s toil and effort, which extend only as far as his own understanding, do not reach such a great attainment as the words of Torah, which are the wisdom of the blessed Lord. When he afterward attains it, he recognizes that it is a find that came when his attention was diverted, and that he did not reach it through his effort. Nevertheless, effort is also necessary: opening an opening the size of a needle’s point through an awakening from below. For the blessed Lord entrusts words of Torah only to those who long for them; of this it is said, “He gives wisdom to the wise.””

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Devarim 32:1:2: “The righteous person is compared to a tree, as it is written, “He shall be like a tree planted beside streams of water, which gives its fruit in its season, and whose leaf does not wither.” A tree produces leaf and fruit; this is a natural property implanted in it on the third day by the utterance, “Let the earth sprout.” The leaf has a purpose, for its shade protects the fruit from the sun’s heat, while the fruit is the essential thing. So too, the righteous person has leaf and fruit. His leaf is his speech about ordinary matters—the affairs of this world, his instruction, and his accounts of events. These are greatly beneficial, just as the leaf that shelters with its shade is beneficial. This is what our Sages expounded: “His leaf does not wither”—even the ordinary conversation of Torah scholars requires study. His fruit is his speech in Torah and wisdom, which is the essential thing, just as fruit is the essential thing in a tree.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: And nonetheless, it is stated at the end of Sefer Heikhalot that even though the Torah had been given, all its sublime virtues—see there seventeen virtues enumerated—did not exist until the Second Temple, despite the Shechinah not dwelling overtly therein.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 17:11: “As is stated explicitly in Sefer Heikhalot, the principal radiance and splendor of Torah were in the Second Temple period, even though the Divine Presence did not rest there. See there the many expressions of praise concerning that time, and how, because they longed for the blessed Lord to reveal the secrets of Torah to them, He promised them this. This is revelation through the wisdom of Oral Torah. They longed for it, to attain still greater understandings, even though it comes through concealment. paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:16:1: ““And it shall be, when I bring a cloud”—a cloud of water, which was the principal element in the generation of the Flood; although there was a flood of fire and water, the principal element stated in Scripture is a flood of water. The Lord promised that there would no longer be a flood, such an overwhelming intensification of desire. This is the meaning of the rainbow appearing: restraint against desire, in the sense of “His bow remained firm.” This is why no rainbow appeared in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s generation: he was on the level of a chasid and did not need restraint, and he was then the foundation of the world, as is stated repeatedly in the Zohar. “Like the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud” is “the appearance of the glory of the Lord.” Glory refers only to Torah, which restrains a person. This is the Lord’s glory: when a person bends his nature and struggles for the sake of the Lord’s will. This is the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 21:1: “As it is written, “The wise inherit honor”—like an inheritance that does not cease, as our Sages said in Bava Metzia 85a: wherever a person is a Torah scholar, and his son, and so forth, it does not cease. “He, his son, and his grandson” means that his wisdom is complete, for a father endows his son with wisdom, as taught at the end of the second chapter of Eduyot, because the son is drawn from the drops of his father’s mind. When wisdom is merely outward speech and is not truly in his depths—when he is wise only in appearance—his wisdom is incomplete, and his son is not a Torah scholar. This is the meaning of their not having recited the blessing over Torah first, as taught in Nedarim 81a: the blessing before Torah is the recognition that wisdom comes from the blessed Lord. Without this, it is merely an illusion and apparent wisdom, not true wisdom. There are two depths in “from the depths,” the hidden mind and heart; the second depth is revealed in the grandson. When wisdom is complete in all its depths, it no longer ceases, and honor is his inheritance.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 27:8-10: “There are two kinds of gratification before Him, blessed be He, on high. One comes from the complete elimination of the other side and the transformation of bitterness into sweetness and darkness into light, through the righteous. The second comes when the other side is subdued while it is still strong and powerful, raising itself like an eagle, and from there the Lord brings it down through the awakening from below brought about by the intermediate person. This is what Scripture says, “Make me delicacies, such as I love.” “Delicacies” is plural: two kinds of gratification. It is the Shekhinah speaking to her children, the collective Israel, as explained in the Tikkunim. By analogy, among physical delicacies there are two kinds: one consists of pleasant, sweet foods; the other of pungent or sour things that have been seasoned and prepared so well that they become delicacies that restore the soul. This is what Scripture says, “The Lord has made everything for His purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil.” It means that he should return from his wickedness and make his evil into day and light above, when the other side is subdued and the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted on high.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part III; Iggeret HaTeshuvah 11:1-2: “As for having humility in his heart—the lower repentance mentioned above—and joy in the Lord, both together: this has already been discussed in Likkutei Amarim at the end of chapter 34, as the holy Zohar says, “Joy is lodged in my heart on this side.” Added to this are faith and trust, so that his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord: He desires kindness, is gracious and compassionate, and abundantly forgives immediately when one asks Him for pardon and forgiveness—“In Your abundant compassion, erase my transgressions”; “Wash me, purify me”; “Erase all my sins”—without any doubt or shadow of doubt whatsoever. Thus, in every Amidah, immediately after asking “Forgive us,” we bless: “Blessed are You, Lord, gracious One who abundantly forgives.” Yet the rule is to be lenient in a case of doubt concerning blessings, because of the concern for a blessing in vain. Rather, there is no doubt here at all, since we have asked, “Forgive us,” “Pardon us.” Had we not returned to sin, we would have been redeemed immediately, as we bless, “Blessed are You, Lord, Redeemer of Israel.””

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:64:1: “This is the difference between the resurrection of the dead and the World to Come. The World to Come is rest from toil: one reaches the utmost level to which one can go, and no further, as they said, “One who did not toil,” and as they said in Berakhot 17a, “The righteous sit”—meaning that they do not proceed to a further level. “And their crowns”: those that they prepared in this world, royal crowns, for the World to Come is the level of kingship, the level of David, peace be upon him, as stated above in section 60. “Upon their heads”: the head is the level of kingship, as in “the heads of the thousands of Israel,” and “David came to the summit,” as explained elsewhere. But in the resurrection of the dead, which is Isaac’s level, as stated there, there is still progression through levels according to what a person is prepared for. That is why they are in bodies, for in the spiritual state there is no progression, as it is written, “I shall give you walkers among these who stand.””

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 43:1: “Nevertheless, in this world there are wicked people to whom things happen as though they had performed the deeds of the righteous, and the reverse. Our Sages said in Berakhot 7b of a wicked person whose hour favors him, “Your judgments are far above, out of his sight.” How can this be, when all His judgments are true? In truth, every person has both merit and guilt. As they said, even the transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvot; and “there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.” Concerning the weighing of merits and sins, Maimonides has already written in the Laws of Repentance that they are weighed only in the knowledge of the blessed Lord. This is certain, for we have no knowledge of it at all. Although our Sages said in many places that one thing is greater than another, they spoke in general terms according to the judgment of Torah. But the judgment above concerns individual souls, and no soul is like another.”

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:17: “Therefore he does not succeed by entering through the lower opening, which is “the gate of the Lord through which the righteous enter,” merely restraining himself because the thing is forbidden. He must raise himself to a higher level, the upper opening: not doing anything that does not give satisfaction and fulfill the will of the blessed Lord. Even if it has become like something permitted to him, he nevertheless recognizes that it is at least not the fulfillment of the blessed Lord’s will. When he takes to heart whether it is the blessed Lord’s will, what desire the blessed Lord has in this, and that he does not wish to do anything that is not His will, he thereby escapes every kind of enticement by the inclination, even in the strongest trial. This accords with the well-known account of what happened to one of the outstanding holy men of the generation before ours. This is the gate through which penitents enter, which is a higher place. It is the lower opening in the first heh of the divine name, while in the final heh it is the upper opening; the lower opening is the gate open to the righteous.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: And therefore King David, peace be upon him, during the preparations for building the Temple—which was likewise "the opening of Your words" with great light, when they donated with a whole heart—opened in prayer: "Keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart unto You" (I Chronicles 29:18), praying that it not depart and be concealed

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Writings, Psalms 69:1: ““But as for me, may my prayer be to You, Lord, at a time of favor.” Sometimes a person feels within himself a great longing and desire to seek the Lord and His strength. At that time he must exert himself in prayer and ask the blessed Lord that this desire remain fixed within him forever. Thus King David, peace be upon him, asked the blessed Lord, when he perceived Israel’s generous-heartedness toward the Temple, “Preserve this forever as the inclination of the thoughts [of Your people’s heart]” (I Chronicles 29:18)—that it never be severed from them. This is the meaning of “A time of favor is significant,” stated in the Gemara (Yevamot 72a).”

quotation.he: ואני תפלתי לך ה' עת רצון. כי לפעמים מרגיש האדם בעצמו חשקות ורצון גדול לדרוש את ה' ועוזו, ואז צריך להתאמץ בתפלה ולבקש מהש"י שישאר זה הרצון קבוע בו לעד, וכמו שדוד המלך עליו השלום בקש מהש"י כאשר הרגיש נדבת לב ישראל לבית המקדש אז אמר (דברי הימים א' כ"ט,י"ח), "שמרה זאת לעולם ליצר מחשבות" כו', היינו שלא ינתק מהם לעד וזה פירוש עת רצון מילתא הוא שנאמר בגמרא (יבמות ע"ב.)
quotation.en: “But as for me, may my prayer be to You, Lord, at a time of favor.” Sometimes a person feels within himself a great longing and desire to seek the Lord and His strength. At that time he must exert himself in prayer and ask the blessed Lord that this desire remain fixed within him forever. Thus King David, peace be upon him, asked the blessed Lord, when he perceived Israel’s generous-heartedness toward the Temple, “Preserve this forever as the inclination of the thoughts [of Your people’s heart]” (I Chronicles 29:18)—that it never be severed from them. This is the meaning of “A time of favor is significant,” stated in the Gemara (Yevamot 72a).

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Shoftim 13:1: “This accords with what I heard from our holy teacher, of righteous and holy memory, concerning the seventh day of Passover. It is said in the Mekhilta, Beshallach, and elsewhere, “A maidservant at the sea saw what Ezekiel did not see.” He said that then they attained only seeing, but not acquisition, until the month of Sivan, the time of the giving of the Torah, when they attained acquisition as well. This is the meaning of the Gemara at the beginning of Bava Metzia: “I might have thought: What does ‘I found it’ mean? ‘I saw it’ … and one acquires through seeing alone.” This is only the Gemara’s initial supposition, and is not the actual conclusion.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 15:9-11: “Through this one can understand the Gemara’s statement that “one who serves God” means someone who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times, while “one who has not served Him” means someone who reviews his chapter only one hundred times. This is because in their days it was customary to review every chapter one hundred times, as the Gemara there illustrates with the market of donkey drivers: they are hired for ten parasangs at one zuz, but for eleven parasangs at two zuz, because this exceeds their usual distance. Therefore this one hundred and first repetition, beyond the habit in which he was trained from his youth, is equal to all the others and surpasses them in excellence and strength, so that he is called “one who serves God.” For to change the nature of habit, he must awaken love of the Lord by contemplating the Lord’s greatness in his mind, in order to rule over the nature in the left chamber, filled with the blood of the animal soul that comes from kelippah, from which this nature derives. This is complete service for the intermediate person. Alternatively, he may awaken the hidden love in his heart in order to rule through it over the nature in the left chamber. This too is called service: to struggle with nature and the inclination by awakening the hidden love in his heart.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 17:1: “Song arises from longing, which is why there are “songs of desire.” When a person’s soul longs entirely for the blessed Lord and is sick with love for Him, his mouth opens to sing before Him. No songs awaken Israel’s love for their Father in Heaven and their union with Him like the Song of Songs. This love is the opposite of love for this world; therefore it is the holy of holies, belonging entirely to the blessed Lord and wholly separated from all the desires of this world, with no connection to them at all. This is the pattern: that same heart which tastes darkness to its furthest limit and seeks the Lord from there tastes light to its furthest limit, until it attains that there is no darkness—“even darkness does not darken,” and “night shines like day.” So it is with all the traits: in the place of a begrudging eye there is a generous eye, and in the place of an evil heart, a good heart.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 37:28-29: “Now, this drawing down and illumination that a person draws and causes to shine from the radiance of the blessed Infinite Light upon his soul and upon the souls of all Israel—which is the Shekhinah, the congregation of Israel, the source of all Israel’s souls, as will be explained below—through the study of Torah is called “calling”: “one who reads in the Torah.” This means that through studying Torah he calls the Holy One, blessed be He, to come to him, as it were, like a person calling his friend to come to him, and like a small child calling his father to come to him, to be together with him and not to separate from him and leave him alone, God forbid. This is the meaning of the verse, “The Lord is close to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth,” and “there is no truth but Torah.” That is, one calls the Holy One, blessed be He, specifically through Torah. This excludes someone who calls Him without studying Torah, but merely cries, “Father! Father!” As the prophet complains about him, “There is no one who calls upon Your name,” as explained elsewhere. From this, the discerning person should reflect so as to draw great awe upon himself while studying Torah, as explained above in chapter 23.”

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:7: “Therefore they said (Eruvin 54b): “Converse”—these are masters of Torah, whose every conversation is Torah. Conversation means speech that is outward, from the lips, as when someone speaks innocently and unreflectively. Thus, at the end of the chapter HaYashen they said: “From Rabban Gamliel’s conversation we learned” (Sukkah 21b). Rabban Gamliel possessed this power in particular, as they said (Eruvin 64b): “From here we learned that Rabban Gamliel discerned correctly through the holy spirit.” The holy spirit means that the speech flows from the supernal holiness mentioned above. paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 52:2: “Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 7b, end): “Serving Torah is greater than studying it.” I heard that study has a limit: how much a person comprehends. Service, however, is the longing and love of the one who serves, which move him to serve and to strive to raise the banner of Torah; this has no limit. He does not comprehend the substance of the Torah revealed to the sages, but only desires and yearns for Torah—that is, for the root of the whole Torah. Thus, service also encompasses the power of the hidden fiftieth gate.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Bechukotai 8:1: ““In His goodness He continually renews the work of creation every day.” This occurs through the new halakhic teaching that the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth each day in the heavenly court (as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 49). paragraphs.text: Sefat Emet, Genesis, Vayera 4:4: “The Holy One’s knowing encompasses a thing from its beginning to its ultimate end, as it is written: “For I have known him, so that he will command his children,” and so forth. Thus, because the righteousness of our father Abraham, of blessed memory, would endure in his descendants, the Omnipresent knew him. The name Elohim means that He is mighty and possesses power; this is easy for the human heart to apprehend and believe. But the aspect of the name Havayah—that He brings everything into being, possesses all powers, and that no power exists apart from Him; that He was, is, and will be; and that “You are He before the world was created, and You are He after the world was created”—is difficult to establish firmly in the human heart, because outward appearances show the opposite.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: and 'in the midst' (be-kerev) hints to the internal organs (keravayim) where worldly digestion takes place; furthermore, through forbidden foods one resembles a beast, as in Zohar II:125b on Nebuchadnezzar, while Daniel who refused defilement with the king's meat was saved from the lions.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 18:9: “The principal preservation of the divine image lies in guarding against forbidden food. Therefore Daniel, who separated himself from their royal food and the wine they drank, was saved from the lions’ den; as stated in the Zohar, “Your fear,” and so forth, was fulfilled in him. For no wild beast rules over a person unless he appears to it as an animal, as stated in Shabbat 151b. This comes about through eating the food of an animal—that is, when one does not recognize that the blessed God feeds and sustains him. Without Him, where would physical food obtain the vitality with which to sustain the soul?”

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:3:1: “At first there must be “fear and love”; afterward the order is reversed: “love and fear,” with love first. For proper worldly conduct precedes Torah. The world was created with the letter bet, which represents fear and constriction, as though there were two: Creator and creature. At first the world was created with the attribute of judgment, and afterward He joined to it the attribute of mercy. Therefore the order of proper worldly conduct is fear and love. This precedes Torah, which is a Torah of kindness and opens with alef, representing love and attachment, as though everything were one. When one reaches Torah, love comes first.”

At first the world was created with the attribute of judgment, and afterward He joined to it the attribute of mercy. Therefore the order of proper worldly conduct is fear and love. This precedes Torah, which is a Torah of kindness and opens with alef, representing love and attachment, as though everything were one. When one reaches Torah, love comes first.

paragraphs.text: Derashot HaRan 8:9: “For this reason Rabbi said: “The reason I surpass my colleagues is that I saw Rabbi Meir from behind. Had I seen him from the front, I would have surpassed them still more, as it is said: ‘Your eyes shall see your teacher’” (Isaiah 30). paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Eikev 17:1: “What is said in the name of our teacher Rabbi Elimelekh, of blessed memory, concerns the Mishnah’s statement: “If my prayer is fluent in my mouth, I know that he has been accepted.” “Fluent” has the sense of being sent: the blessed God sends the prayer into his mouth and takes pride in him, for he is His servant, as explained above. after.enAnchorPrefix: But he never needed this, for never did any extraneous thought enter his mind, having the Blessed Name constantly before his eyes, praying always as one speaking directly before the King of kings.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 31:1: “Isaac came and added that even prayer without deliberate concentration is prayer. This was his level: he would show them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their very eyes (Shabbat 89b)—how the whole earth is filled with His glory, literally present before the eye. With such clear recognition, deliberate concentration of the heart no longer makes a difference, as it says (Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 2:4): “All my days I did not concentrate,” and so forth. For when a person has such clear recognition, this itself is a comprehensive intention encompassing all his thoughts, words, and deeds. Even his ordinary conversation is entirely from the blessed God alone, and there is none besides Him. There is no difference between concentrating this way or that, for which he must make an effort; instead he should leave everything to the blessed God and exert himself only in the fundamental intention, “I have set the Lord before me always”—literally before me. Then, of itself, when he fulfills “Commit,” and so forth, “they shall be established,” and so forth. This is called an unintended act, rather than mere unawareness, for a comprehensive intention is nevertheless required, as explained above, and he must know that he is going to pray.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: and they stated in Yevamot 109b: whoever says he has nothing but Torah does not even possess Torah, for through this he might forget his utter dependence upon Hashem, which is the essence of prayer—the realization that he is deficient, beseeching Hashem to replenish him.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 26:1: “In Torah, the levels are determined by excellence: whoever exceeds his fellow in wisdom is the greater. In prayer, however, the reverse is true: the levels are determined by lack, as stated in the Zohar (I, 23b), “A prayer of the poor,” which envelops all prayers, and as in Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai’s analogy of a servant and a minister (Berakhot 34b). For the more a person lacks and the more he needs, the more he can accomplish through his prayer, because his prayer comes from a deeper place in the heart. The essence of prayer arises from lack, as one asks the blessed God to supply what is missing; before the blessed God there is no distinction between the great and the small.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: For tzitzit is merely a garment enwrapping most of his body, the inner root not yet purified, but wrapped in a mantle of fear of Heaven reminding him at all times not to stray after alien thoughts.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 34:1: “The commandment of tzitzit on one’s garments clothes and covers all the blemishes of the body. The greater part counts as the whole, and therefore wrapping the head and most of the body is sufficient: through this, the whole person is completely covered, so that no creature recognizes what is in his heart—only the blessed God alone—and there is no place for accusation.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 16:1: “In every new Torah teaching, a matter cannot be so fully determined that there is no inclination in either direction, as it says (Ḥagigah 3b): “These declare impure,” and so forth; and “these and those are the words of the living God” (Eruvin 13b). Elohim means the Possessor of all the distinct powers in the world, and therefore it is a plural expression. “Living,” too, is plural, for words of Torah are the life of the whole creation, and life has different divisions. Of this it is said: “Like streams of water, a king’s heart is in the hand,” and so forth. Who are the kings? The rabbis (Gittin 62a); and water means Torah (Bava Kamma 17a). They divide into different springs, to prohibit and to permit. We think that this depends upon the sage’s own mind, but it is not so: this too is in the hand of the Lord, who illuminates his eyes and inclines his heart solely according to the divine desire and will.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Hashanah 15:1: “As we heard from our holy teacher of Izbica, of blessed memory, concerning “The Lord was not in the wind”: that a person has a desire for holiness does not yet establish certainty. “The Lord was not in the tumult”: even when one possesses alacrity and vigor. “The Lord was not in the fire”: even when one has fervor in the pursuit of holy service. None of these yet establishes certainty. Only “after the fire, a still, thin voice”—these three words are the blessed God’s signature upon the three qualities found in the souls of Israel: wind, tumult, and fire. Then a person can trust in the name of the Lord, but cannot rely on anything that comes from himself.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Korach 1:2: “This was Korah’s mistake: at the giving of the Torah, the true repair that will exist in the future should indeed have occurred. This was his claim: “For the whole congregation are all holy”—all heard “I am the Lord your God” at Sinai, as stated in Bemidbar Rabbah—“and the Lord is among them.” That is, as it will be in the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits among them and they surround Him in a circle, as explained; in a circle there are no ranks, as stated above. Thus, “Why do you exalt yourselves over the congregation of the Lord?” This is indeed so when the attribute of Atika is revealed, as it was at the giving of the Torah, where it is written: “Face to face the Lord spoke with you.” Similarly, the revelation at the splitting of the Sea was also from the attribute of Atika, as stated in the holy Zohar (II, 52b), that it depends upon Atika. The Mekhilta and the holy Zohar there (64b) state: “A maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see.” This means that the maidservant saw as much as the greatest person in Israel: all were equal, because when it depends upon Atika there are no ranks. So too at the giving of the Torah, as it says, “Israel encamped there,” which Rashi explains as “like one person, with one heart.” There were no ranks, as it says, “Face to face the Lord spoke with you.” But afterward this level ceased, and this revelation will not occur again until the future, which is the true repair.”

quotation.he: וזה היה טעות קרח שכיון שבאמת בשעת מתן תורה היה ראוי להיות התיקון האמיתי כמו שיהיה לעתיד. וזה שטען כי כל העדה כולם קדושים וכולם שמעו בסיני אנכי ה' אלהיך (כמ"ש במ"ר) ובתוכם ה' והיינו כמו שיהיה לעתיד שהקב"ה יושב ביניהם והם סביב במחול וכאמור ובעיגול אין שום מדריגות כנ"ל ומדוע תתנשאו על קהל ה'. וכן הוא באמת כשיש התגלות מדת עתיקא כמו שהי' ההתגלות בשעת מתן תורה דכתיב פנים בפנים דבר ה' עמכם. וכמו ההתגלות שהיה בקריעות ים סוף שהיה גם כן ממדת עתיקא כמ"ש בזוהר הקדוש (ח"ב נ"ב ב') דבעתיקא תליא ואיתא במכילתא ובזוהר הקדוש שם ס"ד ב') ראתה שפחה על הים מה שלא ראה יחזקאל היינו שהשפחה ראתה כמו הגדול שבישראל הכל שוים כיון דבעתיקא תליא אז אין שום מדרגות וכן היה במתן תורה גם כן וכמו שנאמר שם ויחן שם ישראל ופירש"י כאיש אחד בלב אחד ולא היה מדרגות כמו שנאמר פנים בפנים דיבר ה' עמכם אבל אחר כך נתבטל מדרגה זו ולא יהיה ההתגלות הזה עד לעתיד שזה התיקון האמיתי.
quotation.en: This was Korah’s mistake: at the giving of the Torah, the true repair that will exist in the future should indeed have occurred. This was his claim: “For the whole congregation are all holy”—all heard “I am the Lord your God” at Sinai, as stated in Bemidbar Rabbah—“and the Lord is among them.” That is, as it will be in the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits among them and they surround Him in a circle, as explained; in a circle there are no ranks, as stated above. Thus, “Why do you exalt yourselves over the congregation of the Lord?” This is indeed so when the attribute of Atika is revealed, as it was at the giving of the Torah, where it is written: “Face to face the Lord spoke with you.” Similarly, the revelation at the splitting of the Sea was also from the attribute of Atika, as stated in the holy Zohar (II, 52b), that it depends upon Atika. The Mekhilta and the holy Zohar there (64b) state: “A maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see.” This means that the maidservant saw as much as the greatest person in Israel: all were equal, because when it depends upon Atika there are no ranks. So too at the giving of the Torah, as it says, “Israel encamped there,” which Rashi explains as “like one person, with one heart.” There were no ranks, as it says, “Face to face the Lord spoke with you.” But afterward this level ceased, and this revelation will not occur again until the future, which is the true repair.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Pesach 30:1: “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world is so that a person should derive from it instruction for serving the Lord, for He created everything for His glory. As was said in the name of the holy master of Peshischa, of blessed memory, concerning the name Shaddai, “who said to His world: Enough”: it is sufficient for learning to recognize the blessed God. When our father Abraham, of blessed memory, came and saw a palace ablaze, he wondered: Is it possible for the palace to have no governor? Until the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him and said: “I am the owner of the palace,” as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 39. He explained through this the verse “The earth is full of Your possessions”: the whole earth is filled with acquisitions through which a person may acquire knowledge of the blessed God and of what the blessed God wants from him. Everything that comes before a person’s eyes has been deliberately brought before him by particular providence, so that he should learn from it.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 13:1: “As is known, whenever one person has experienced the clear illumination of a matter in its fullness, the gate of that light has already been opened in the world. It remains open afterward to everyone. This is the whole purpose of the succession of generations established by the blessed God, even though they become progressively smaller. For all the lights opened in each generation by outstanding individuals among the sages of Israel are never closed again. They remain open forever and become established teachings for all Israel. Therefore, although the later generations are smaller, they nevertheless possess the advantage of a dwarf upon a giant: all the gates opened by earlier generations already stand open before them, and they continue to bring forth new teaching and open other gates. Although they are very small, they nevertheless reach deeper places, for their souls have already passed through the gate that was opened for the earlier generations.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: In a matter where a person is deficient and requires rectification by means of behaving in the opposite extreme,

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Human Dispositions 2:2: “What is their cure? A person prone to anger is told to train himself so that even if he is struck and cursed, he takes no notice at all. He should follow this course for a long time, until anger is uprooted from his heart. If he is haughty, he should conduct himself with great self-abasement: sit below everyone, wear worn-out rags that bring their wearer into contempt, and do similar things, until haughtiness is uprooted from him and he returns to the middle way, which is the good way. Once he returns to the middle way, he should follow it all his days. He should proceed along these lines with all the other character traits: if he has gone far toward one extreme, he should move far toward the other extreme and conduct himself that way for a long time, until he returns to the good way, which is the intermediate measure in every character trait.”

after.enAnchorPrefix: Likewise wisdom, even though it operates in concealment, is a greater perception than prophecy.

paragraphs.text:
Gevurot Hashem, Introduction to Gevurot Hashem 4-6: “There is a difference between wisdom and prophecy. The sage apprehends through his intellect, and because he apprehends through his intellect, he can apprehend the most hidden and concealed things. The prophet, however, is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer’: seeing applies when someone sees a thing from outside. Every prophet must therefore have a connection to the matter concerning which he prophesies. He connects himself to those things and knows them through his prophecy.

The Sages therefore said, ‘A sage is greater than a prophet.’ The explanation is that prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which perceives its object from outside. Although prophecy does not come through the perception of a physical sense, nevertheless, just as a sense connects with its object, so the prophet’s power of prophecy—the imaginative faculty, or whatever faculty receives prophecy—connects with the thing about which he prophesies. For this reason the sage is greater: he apprehends and knows hidden matters and brings them forth from his own intellect. Because of this difference, the prophet is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer,’ whereas the sage is not. It is therefore impossible for the matter of the World to Come and the soul’s continued existence to enter prophecy at all, since ‘seeing’ or ‘vision’ does not apply to them. This matter is separate from the human being; because it is completely separate from him, prophecy does not apply to it. We have already explained that prophecy requires an external connection with that about which one prophesies. The World to Come and the soul’s continued existence are therefore explained more fully through wisdom—for the sage apprehends hidden matters—than through prophecy. Thus ‘a sage is greater than a prophet,’ because he can apprehend something that cannot be apprehended through prophecy. The power of prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which receives its objects from outside. How, then, could the matter of the World to Come be written in the Torah, when it does not belong to the domain of prophecy? Anyone who knows the distinction between the sage and the prophet knows that this is impossible, for the prophets connected themselves with the things about which they prophesied.

The Sages therefore said: ‘All the prophets prophesied only concerning the days of the Messiah; but concerning the World to Come, “No eye has seen, O God, except You.”’ The explanation is that since prophecy requires seeing—an external connection with what is known through prophecy—the prophets could prophesy only concerning the days of the Messiah. The matter of the Messiah belongs to this world and is not completely separate from the human being, for it is in this world. But there is no prophecy concerning the World to Come, which is separate from this world, for no eye has seen it. The prophet prophesies only through seeing, as has been explained.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: כי הפרש יש בין החכמה ובין הנבואה; כי החכם ישיג מצד שכלו, ומכיון שהוא ישיג מצד שכלו, יוכל להשיג הדברים הנעלמים והנסתרים ביותר. אבל הנביא יקרא "חוזה" (מ"ב יז, יג), או "רואה" (ש"א ט, ט), ששייך רואה במה שהוא רואה הדבר מבחוץ. לכך צריך לכל נביא התדבקות בדבר לאשר נבואתו בו, והוא מתדבק בדברים ההם, וידעם מפני נבואתו. ולפיכך אמרו חכמים (ב"ב יב.) 'חכם עדיף מנביא'. וביאור זה, כי הנבואה דומה כדבר לחוש עין, שירגיש המוחש מבחוץ. ואף כי אין הנבואה על ידי השגת החוש הגשמי, מכל מקום כמו שהחוש דבק במוחש, כך יש התדבקות כח הנבואה של הנביא, שהוא כח המדמה, או מה שהוא הכח המקבל הנבואה, שהוא מתדבק בדבר שהוא מתנבא עליו. ומפני זה יותר עדיף החכם, אשר הוא משיג ויודע הדברים הנעלמים, ומוציא אותם משכלו מעצמו. ומפני ההבדל הזה יקרא הנביא "חוזה" או "רואה", מה שאין כך בחכם. ולפיכך אי אפשר שיבא כלל ענין עולם הבא והשארת נפש בנבואה, כיון שלא שייך בזה רואה או חוזה, כי דבר זה נבדל מן האדם, ולפי שהוא נבדל לגמרי מן האדם, לא תפול הנבואה בו. שכבר אמרנו כי הנבואה צריך להתדבקות מבחוץ במה שהוא מתנבא עליו. לכך עולם הבא והשארת הנפש יתבאר יותר בחכמה, שהחכם משיג הדברים הנעלמים, יותר ממה שיתבאר בנבואה. לכך "חכם עדיף מנביא", מה שהוא יכול להשיג דבר שאי אפשר בנבואה. שכח הנבואה מתדמה לחוש העין המקבל מוחשיו מבחוץ, ואיך אפשר להיות נכתב בתורה ענין עולם הבא, שאין זה מענין הנבואה. כי מי שידע החילוק אשר יש בין החכם ובין הנביא, ידע כי אי אפשר דבר זה, כי הנביאים היו מתדבקים בדבר שהיו מתנבאים עליו. ולפיכך אמרו חכמים (ברכות לד:), כל הנביאים לא נתנבאו אלא לימי המשיח, אבל עולם הבא "עין לא ראתה אלוהים זולתך" (ישעיה סד, ג). ביאור ענין זה, כי מאחר שצריך לנבואה ראיה, והיא התדבקות מבחוץ במה שידע מן הנבואה, לא היו יכולים להתנבאות רק לימות המשיח, במה שענין המשיח הוא ענין עולם הזה, ואינו נבדל מן האדם לגמרי, שהרי הוא בעולם הזה. אבל עולם הבא שנבדל מן העולם הזה, אין בו נבואה, כי עין לא ראתה אותו, ואין הנביא מתנבא רק בראיה, כמו שהתבאר.
