'חכם עדיף מנביא'. וביאור זה, כי הנבואה דומה כדבר לחוש עין, שירגיש המוחש מבחוץ. ואף כי אין הנבואה על ידי השגת החוש הגשמי, מכל מקום כמו שהחוש דבק במוחש, כך יש התדבקות כח הנבואה של הנביא, שהוא כח המדמה, או מה שהוא הכח המקבל הנבואה, שהוא מתדבק בדבר שהוא מתנבא עליו. ומפני זה יותר עדיף החכם, אשר הוא משיג ויודע הדברים הנעלמים, ומוציא אותם משכלו מעצמו. ומפני ההבדל הזה יקרא הנביא "חוזה" או "רואה", מה שאין כך בחכם. ולפיכך אי אפשר שיבא כלל ענין עולם הבא והשארת נפש בנבואה, כיון שלא שייך בזה רואה או חוזה, כי דבר זה נבדל מן האדם, ולפי שהוא נבדל לגמרי מן האדם, לא תפול הנבואה בו. שכבר אמרנו כי הנבואה צריך להתדבקות מבחוץ במה שהוא מתנבא עליו. לכך עולם הבא והשארת הנפש יתבאר יותר בחכמה, שהחכם משיג הדברים הנעלמים, יותר ממה שיתבאר בנבואה. לכך "חכם עדיף מנביא", מה שהוא יכול להשיג דבר שאי אפשר בנבואה. שכח הנבואה מתדמה לחוש העין המקבל מוחשיו מבחוץ, ואיך אפשר להיות נכתב בתורה ענין עולם הבא, שאין זה מענין הנבואה. כי מי שידע החילוק אשר יש בין החכם ובין הנביא, ידע כי אי אפשר דבר זה, כי הנביאים היו מתדבקים בדבר שהיו מתנבאים עליו. ולפיכך אמרו חכמים (ברכות לד:), כל הנביאים לא נתנבאו אלא לימי המשיח, אבל עולם הבא "עין לא ראתה אלוהים זולתך" (ישעיה סד, ג). ביאור ענין זה, כי מאחר שצריך לנבואה ראיה, והיא התדבקות מבחוץ במה שידע מן הנבואה, לא היו יכולים להתנבאות רק לימות המשיח, במה שענין המשיח הוא ענין עולם הזה, ואינו נבדל מן האדם לגמרי, שהרי הוא בעולם הזה. אבל עולם הבא שנבדל מן העולם הזה, אין בו נבואה, כי עין לא ראתה אותו, ואין הנביא מתנבא רק בראיה, כמו שהתבאר.
quotation.en:
There is a difference between wisdom and prophecy. The sage apprehends through his intellect, and because he apprehends through his intellect, he can apprehend the most hidden and concealed things. The prophet, however, is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer’: seeing applies when someone sees a thing from outside. Every prophet must therefore have a connection to the matter concerning which he prophesies. He connects himself to those things and knows them through his prophecy.

The Sages therefore said, ‘A sage is greater than a prophet.’ The explanation is that prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which perceives its object from outside. Although prophecy does not come through the perception of a physical sense, nevertheless, just as a sense connects with its object, so the prophet’s power of prophecy—the imaginative faculty, or whatever faculty receives prophecy—connects with the thing about which he prophesies. For this reason the sage is greater: he apprehends and knows hidden matters and brings them forth from his own intellect. Because of this difference, the prophet is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer,’ whereas the sage is not. It is therefore impossible for the matter of the World to Come and the soul’s continued existence to enter prophecy at all, since ‘seeing’ or ‘vision’ does not apply to them. This matter is separate from the human being; because it is completely separate from him, prophecy does not apply to it. We have already explained that prophecy requires an external connection with that about which one prophesies. The World to Come and the soul’s continued existence are therefore explained more fully through wisdom—for the sage apprehends hidden matters—than through prophecy. Thus ‘a sage is greater than a prophet,’ because he can apprehend something that cannot be apprehended through prophecy. The power of prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which receives its objects from outside. How, then, could the matter of the World to Come be written in the Torah, when it does not belong to the domain of prophecy? Anyone who knows the distinction between the sage and the prophet knows that this is impossible, for the prophets connected themselves with the things about which they prophesied.

The Sages therefore said: ‘All the prophets prophesied only concerning the days of the Messiah; but concerning the World to Come, “No eye has seen, O God, except You.”’ The explanation is that since prophecy requires seeing—an external connection with what is known through prophecy—the prophets could prophesy only concerning the days of the Messiah. The matter of the Messiah belongs to this world and is not completely separate from the human being, for it is in this world. But there is no prophecy concerning the World to Come, which is separate from this world, for no eye has seen it. The prophet prophesies only through seeing, as has been explained.

Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 2:1-7: “Here is the answer to the heretics, and the exposure of the root of the error of those who deny individual providence and the signs and wonders of the Torah. In their false imagination they mistakenly compare Hashem’s work—‘the Maker of heaven and earth’—to human work and craftsmanship. Once a vessel has left the craftsman’s hands, it no longer needs him: even when his hands have withdrawn from it and he goes away to the market, the vessel remains in precisely the form and shape it had when it left his hands. These foolish people imagine the making of heaven and earth in the same way.

But ‘their eyes are shut against seeing’ the great difference between human work and craftsmanship, which make something from something already existing—merely changing its form and shape from a piece of silver into a vessel—and the making of heaven and earth, which brings something into being from nothing.

This is a greater wonder than, for example, the splitting of the Red Sea. ‘Hashem drove the sea back with a strong east wind all that night, and the waters were divided’; they ‘stood like a heap’ and like a wall. Had Hashem stopped the wind for a moment, the water would have returned and flowed downward in its usual, natural way, and would certainly not have remained standing like a wall. This is so even though this nature of water was itself created and brought into being from nothing: a stone wall stands by itself without wind, but the nature of water is different.

All the more so with creation from nothing, which transcends nature and is an even greater wonder than the splitting of the Red Sea. If the Creator’s power were to withdraw from the created being, Heaven forbid, the created being would return to actual nothingness and nonexistence. Rather, the power of the maker must remain continually within what is made, giving it life and sustaining it. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Of this it is said, ‘You give life to them all.’ Read not merely ‘give life’ but ‘bring into being’—that is, bring something into being from nothing. ‘You’—atah—signifies the letters from alef to tav, while the hei signifies the five organs of speech, the source of the letters. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Although He has no bodily likeness, Scripture states explicitly, ‘Hashem spoke’ and ‘Hashem said.’ This is the revelation of the twenty-two supernal letters to the prophets. They are clothed in the prophets’ intellect and comprehension in the prophetic vision, and also in their thought and speech, as it is written: ‘The spirit of Hashem spoke through me, and His word was upon my tongue,’ and as the Ari, of blessed memory, explained in the Gate of Prophecy.

The letters are similarly clothed in created beings, as it is written: ‘By the word of Hashem the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.’ This, however, takes place through numerous and immense stages of descent, until the letters descend into physical action. By contrast, the prophets’ apprehension is in Atzilut as it is clothed in the World of Beriah.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: והנה, מכאן תשובת המינים וגילוי שורש טעותם, הכופרים בהשגחה פרטית ובאותות ומופתי התורה, שטועים בדמיונם הכוזב, שמדמין מעשה ה׳ – ״עושה שמים וארץ״ למעשה אנוש ותחבולותיו, כי כאשר יצא לצורף כלי – שוב אין הכלי צריך לידי הצורף, כי אף שידיו מסולקות הימנו והולך לו בשוק – הכלי קיים בתבניתו וצלמו ממש כאשר יצא מידי הצורף, כך מדמין הסכלים האלו מעשה שמים וארץ. אך ״טח מראות עיניהם״, ההבדל הגדול שבין מעשה אנוש ותחבולותיו, שהוא יש מיש, רק שמשנה הצורה והתמונה מתמונת חתיכת כסף לתמונת כלי, למעשה שמים וארץ, שהוא יש מאין. והוא פלא גדול יותר מקריעת ים סוף על דרך משל, ש״הוליך ה׳ את הים ברוח קדים עזה כל הלילה ויבקעו המים״, ו״נצבו כמו נד״ וכחומה ואילו הפסיק ה׳ את הרוח כרגע – היו המים חוזרים וניגרים במורד כדרכם וטבעם, ולא קמו כחומה בלי ספק, אף שהטבע הזה במים גם כן נברא ומחודש יש מאין, שהרי חומת אבנים נצבת מעצמה בלי רוח, רק שטבע המים אינו כן. וכל שכן וקל וחומר בבריאת יש מאין, שהיא למעלה מהטבע, והפלא ופלא יותר מקריעת ים סוף, על אחת כמה וכמה שבהסתלקות כח הבורא מן הנברא חס ושלום – ישוב הנברא לאין ואפס ממש. אלא צריך להיות כח הפועל בנפעל תמיד, להחיותו ולקיימו. והן הן בחינות אותיות הדבור מעשרה מאמרות שבהם נבראו. ועל זה נאמר: ״ואתה מחיה את כולם״ – אל תקרי ״מחיה״, אלא ״מהוה״, דהיינו, יש מאין, ו״אתה״ – הן בחינות האותיות מאל״ף ועד תי״ו, והה״א – היא ה׳ מוצאות הפה, מקור האותיות. והן הן בחינות אותיות הדבור מעשרה מאמרות שבהם נבראו. ואף שאין לו דמות הגוף – הרי מקרא מלא דבר הכתוב: ״וידבר ה׳״, ״ויאמר ה׳״, והיא בחינת התגלות הכ״ב אותיות עליונות לנביאים, ומתלבשות בשכלם והשגתם במראה הנבואה, וגם במחשבתם ודיבורם, כמו שכתוב: ״רוח ה׳ דבר בי, ומלתו על לשוני״, וכמו שאמר האר״י זכרונו לברכה [בשער הנבואה]. וכעין זה היא התלבשות האותיות בברואים, כדכתיב: ״בדבר ה׳ שמים נעשו, וברוח פיו כל צבאם״, רק, שהיא על ידי השתלשלות רבות ועצומות, עד שיורדות לעשיה גופנית, מה שאין כן השגת הנביאים, היא באצילות המתלבשת בעולם הבריאה:

Once a vessel has left the craftsman’s hands, it no longer needs him: even when his hands have withdrawn from it and he goes away to the market, the vessel remains in precisely the form and shape it had when it left his hands. These foolish people imagine the making of heaven and earth in the same way.

But ‘their eyes are shut against seeing’ the great difference between human work and craftsmanship, which make something from something already existing—merely changing its form and shape from a piece of silver into a vessel—and the making of heaven and earth, which brings something into being from nothing.

This is a greater wonder than, for example, the splitting of the Red Sea. ‘Hashem drove the sea back with a strong east wind all that night, and the waters were divided’; they ‘stood like a heap’ and like a wall. Had Hashem stopped the wind for a moment, the water would have returned and flowed downward in its usual, natural way, and would certainly not have remained standing like a wall. This is so even though this nature of water was itself created and brought into being from nothing: a stone wall stands by itself without wind, but the nature of water is different.

All the more so with creation from nothing, which transcends nature and is an even greater wonder than the splitting of the Red Sea. If the Creator’s power were to withdraw from the created being, Heaven forbid, the created being would return to actual nothingness and nonexistence. Rather, the power of the maker must remain continually within what is made, giving it life and sustaining it. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Of this it is said, ‘You give life to them all.’ Read not merely ‘give life’ but ‘bring into being’—that is, bring something into being from nothing. ‘You’—atah—signifies the letters from alef to tav, while the hei signifies the five organs of speech, the source of the letters. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Although He has no bodily likeness, Scripture states explicitly, ‘Hashem spoke’ and ‘Hashem said.’ This is the revelation of the twenty-two supernal letters to the prophets. They are clothed in the prophets’ intellect and comprehension in the prophetic vision, and also in their thought and speech, as it is written: ‘The spirit of Hashem spoke through me, and His word was upon my tongue,’ and as the Ari, of blessed memory, explained in the Gate of Prophecy.

The letters are similarly clothed in created beings, as it is written: ‘By the word of Hashem the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.’ This, however, takes place through numerous and immense stages of descent, until the letters descend into physical action. By contrast, the prophets’ apprehension is in Atzilut as it is clothed in the World of Beriah.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Nasso 4: “‘They shall send from the camp every person afflicted with tzaraat, every person with a discharge, and everyone impure through contact with a corpse.’ A person afflicted with tzaraat represents anger, for tzaraat comes as punishment for evil speech. A person with a discharge represents one ruled by desire, and impurity through a corpse represents sadness. Therefore the person afflicted with tzaraat is sent out of all three camps, for the trait of anger has no share in Israel. The person with a discharge is sent out only from the Levite camp and the camp of the Divine Presence, for the trait of desire is unfitting for Torah scholars. The person impure through a corpse is sent out only from the camp of the Divine Presence, for the trait of sadness is sometimes found even among Torah scholars, as the Gemara says: ‘It is the Torah that makes him seethe’; this seething is sadness. He is therefore sent out only from the camp of the Divine Presence, for ‘strength and joy are in His place.’”

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part III; Iggeret HaTeshuvah 6:7-11: “It is written, ‘Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.’ By way of analogy, a cord has one end above and its other end below. If a person pulls the lower end, he also moves and draws the upper end after it, as far as it can be drawn.

Exactly so with the root and source of a person’s soul in the lower hei mentioned above: through his evil deeds and thoughts, he draws its influence down, as it were, into the chambers of the other side, from which his thoughts and deeds derive. Since he is the one who draws this influence to them, he takes the first share; this is sufficient for one who understands.

This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, meant by saying, ‘Neither the tranquility of the wicked, and so forth, is in our hands.’ ‘In our hands’ is precise: it means during the exile after the destruction of the Temple. This is the exile of the Divine Presence, as it were: to bestow influence upon the chambers of the other side, which His blessed soul abhors.

When a person repents properly, he removes from them the influence that he drew down through his deeds and thoughts, for through his repentance he restores the influence of the Divine Presence to its proper place.

This is the return of the lower hei from exile. As it is written, ‘Hashem your God will return with your captivity’—that is, together with your captivity. As our Sages, of blessed memory, said: ‘It does not say, “He will bring back,”’ and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 35:4: “The explanation of this analogy—which compares the light of the Divine Presence to a lamp’s light, which neither shines nor takes hold of the wick without oil—is clear and understandable to every discerning person. Similarly, the Divine Presence rests upon the human body, which is compared to a wick, specifically through good deeds. The soul, although it is a portion of God above, does not by itself suffice to serve as oil for the wick. Even the soul of a completely righteous person, who serves Hashem with awe and a love of delights, is not wholly nullified out of existence so as to be nullified and incorporated within the actual light of Hashem, becoming one with it in complete unity. Rather, he remains a distinct being who fears Hashem and loves Him. This is unlike the commandments and good deeds, which are His blessed will. His blessed will is the source of life for all worlds and created beings; it descends to them through many contractions, through concealment of the countenance of the supernal will, blessed be He, and through successive levels of descent, until they can come into being and be created from nothing as separate entities, without being nullified out of existence, as explained above. The commandments, however, are the inner dimension of His blessed will, where there is no concealment of the countenance at all. Their life-force is therefore not a separate entity at all, but is united with and incorporated within His blessed will, becoming truly one with it in complete unity.”

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 37:6-8: “Likewise, the power of the vital, animal soul in the bodily limbs of the person performing the commandment is clothed in this action. It rises out of the kelipah, is incorporated within the holiness of the commandment, which is His blessed will, and is nullified within the light of the blessed Infinite.

Even with the commandments of Torah study, reciting the Shema, prayer, and the like, although they do not involve actual physical action under the dominion of kelipat nogah, we nevertheless hold that thought is not equivalent to speech: a person does not discharge his obligation until he expresses the words with his lips. We also hold that moving one’s lips counts as an action. For the divine soul cannot express itself through the physical lips, mouth, tongue, and teeth except by means of the vital, animal soul that is actually clothed in the bodily limbs. The more forcefully a person speaks, the more powers of the vital soul he invests and clothes in these words.

This is what Scripture means by, ‘All my bones shall say,’ and so forth. It is also what our Sages, of blessed memory, meant: ‘If it is ordered in all 248 limbs, it is retained; if not, it is not retained.’ Forgetfulness comes from the kelipah of the body and the vital, animal soul, which derive from kelipat nogah. They are sometimes incorporated within holiness: this happens when a person exhausts their power and invests all their strength in the holiness of Torah or prayer.”

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 7:1-5: “The vital, animal soul in Israel that comes from the kelipah and is clothed in a person’s blood, as explained above; the souls of ritually pure domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and fish that may be eaten; the existence and vitality of all inanimate matter and all vegetation that may be consumed; and likewise the existence and vitality of every deed, word, and thought concerning this world that involves no prohibition—neither a root nor a branch of the 365 negative commandments or their biblical or rabbinic extensions—but is not for the sake of Heaven, and instead expresses the body’s will, desire, and appetite: all these belong to the same category. Even if something is actually necessary for the body’s existence and vitality, if one’s intention is not for the sake of Heaven, to serve Hashem with one’s body, these deeds, words, and thoughts are no better than the vital, animal soul itself. All of them alike receive and draw their vitality from the second level among the kelipot and the other side: the fourth kelipah, called kelipat nogah. In this world, called the World of Asiyah, it is almost entirely evil, with only a little good mixed into it. From it come the good traits of the animal soul in Israel, as explained above.

It is an intermediate condition between the three completely impure kelipot and the condition and level of holiness.

Therefore it is sometimes incorporated within the three impure kelipot, as stated in Etz Chayim, Gate 49, at the beginning of chapter 4, in the name of the Zohar. At other times it is incorporated within and ascends to the condition and level of holiness: namely, when the good mixed into it is separated from the evil, prevails, and ascends to become incorporated within holiness.

For example, someone eats rich beef and drinks fragrant wine to broaden his mind for Hashem and His Torah, as Rava said, ‘Wine and fragrance,’ and so forth; or he does so to fulfill the commandment of delighting in Shabbat and the festivals. The vitality of the meat and wine, which had flowed from kelipat nogah, is then refined and ascends to Hashem like a burnt offering and sacrifice.

The same applies to someone who says something humorous to open his mind and gladden his heart for Hashem, His Torah, and His service, which must be undertaken joyfully. This is what Rava did for his students: he first said something humorous before them, and the Sages were cheered.”
